summary.headline: AU SFB Q4 FY26 profit rose 65% YoY to ₹832 crore with ROA 1.8%, but management guided FY27 credit cost near 0.90% and flagged margin pressure.
summary.overview: AU Small Finance Bank reported a strong Q4 FY26, with PAT up 25% QoQ and 65% YoY to ₹832 crore and quarterly ROA of 1.8%, helped by seasonal factors. Deposits grew 10% QoQ and 23% YoY, and loans grew 8% QoQ and 21% YoY, both ahead of the stated private sector benchmark of 13%. Slippages fell 17% QoQ to ₹659 crore and GNPA improved to 2.03%. Management said Q4 was flattered by seasonality, a day-count benefit and lower reversals, and that cost of funds may have bottomed after recent rate hikes.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost to assets (FY26, excl. CGFMU premium)

segments.name: Retail secured (wheels, mortgages, gold)
segments.commentary: Retail secured is 66% of portfolio and grew 21% YoY. Wheels reached about ₹46,400 crore (+27% YoY), gold loans about ₹4,000 crore (doubled), and mortgages (micro business and affordable housing) about ₹42,400 crore (+11% YoY).

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Commercial banking is 22% of lending, at about ₹31,000 crore (+29% YoY, +12% QoQ), plus about ₹11,000 crore of non-fund book. It currently funds about 56% of its requirement internally, with a goal of full self-funding alongside transaction banking and CMS.

segments.name: Inclusive banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Inclusive banking grew 8% QoQ. Non-overdue collection efficiency in MFI was 99.7% (vs 99.3% in Q3), and 92% of the MFI book is covered under CGFMU.

segments.name: Digital unsecured (cards and personal loans)
segments.commentary: Digital unsecured grew 4% QoQ. Personal loans rose 19% QoQ from a low base, and credit cards broadly stabilised after about five quarters of decline. Total unsecured fell 1% YoY.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits reached ₹1.52 lakh crore (+10% QoQ, +23% YoY). CASA grew 9% QoQ and 20% YoY, with CASA ratio about 28%. Branch banking is about 60% of deposits, and stable deposits are 79%.

guidance_outlook: Management guided FY27 credit cost of around 0.90% of average assets, and said Q4's 0.6% should not be used as the run-rate.
Full-year FY27 cost to assets is expected to fall below 4%, from 4.1% in FY26.
Cost of funds may have bottomed after recent rate hikes. Seasonal margin benefits from Q4 are not expected to recur in the next one to two quarters, implying margin pressure.
Asset mix shift toward secured assets may pressure yields, as unsecured grows slower than the rest of the book.
Management aims to grow at 2 to 2.5x nominal GDP, and said 1.8% ROA is not a permanent level. Its goal is to hold ROA around 1.8% on a full-year basis next year.
Universal bank licence: final application filed in March 2026, pending regulatory approval. Fincare core banking migration completed in April 2026.
capex_capacity: Plans to open 80 to 100 branches every year, with 2,790 touchpoints cited on the call (the 2,500 figure was corrected).
Retail secured distribution has nearly doubled in two years to about 900 to 1,000 branches per retail secured business.
First AI-native loan origination system (gold loans) went live the week before the call. Expansion to mortgages, commercial banking, wheels, personal loans and credit card LOS is underway.
Outbound AI-led calling campaigns aim to reach 25% of total calls over the next two quarters.
Organisational consolidation: agri merged into business banking, and home loans and MBL share back-end teams.
demand_pricing: Management said the home loan/affordable housing market is too competitive, with new NBFCs and HFCs entering, so it is not growing there irrationally.

Deposit rates on savings and term deposits were raised ahead of peers. Management said this reflects the mix of retail vs wholesale, CASA and CD ratio targets, and that it will be managed monthly through ALCO.
Long-term cost-of-funds aspiration is to trade near the prevailing repo rate (5.25% currently), against about 6.75% now.
Wheels growth was driven by improving affordability across segments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the details of the ₹21 crore contingency provision created in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said these were ordinary business banking working-capital standard accounts, not high-value specific cases. The provision was added on an internal risk assessment of security cover, with no specific segment or aggregate exposure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why were savings and term deposit rates raised well ahead of the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said it is a combination of how much to raise, cost of money, CASA and retail/wholesale mix and CD ratio. He noted cost of money fell 32 bps in FY26 against an expected 15-20 bps, and that liabilities are managed daily and monthly through ALCO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable ROA and what levers drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said Q4 is seasonally strong and the aim is to hold ROA around 1.8% on a full-year basis next year. Levers are opex-to-assets improvement and lower credit costs from MFI and credit cards. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin was from IT refund and other one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said the IT refund helped only slightly and was not material. He said cost of funds may have bottomed, and the seasonal benefits from lower day count and lower slippages will not recur next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How should cost-to-assets evolve as the bank moves to a universal banking licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said FY27 cost to assets should go below 4%, with a first benchmark of about 3.5% in three to five years. He declined to give a number for AI-driven cost savings, calling the technology too early-stage to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost should be assumed going forward, and how will the new RBI ECL norms affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal suggested building credit cost around 0.90%, and said Q4 should not be annualised. On ECL, management said it was too early to comment. Vivek Tripathi said 90% of the book is secured and CGFMU covers MFI, and the guideline applies from April 2027.

risks_watch: Margin compression as the Q4 seasonal benefits reverse and cost of funds may have bottomed after the rate hike.
Credit cost normalisation toward the 0.90% guidance from 0.6% in Q4, with the MFI and credit card recovery still at an early stage.
ECL transition from April 2027 and its impact on provisioning and PCR (PCR excluding the credit guarantee book is about 70%).
Deposit pricing pressure from ongoing savings and term deposit rate hikes, and whether the CASA ratio of 28% holds.
Management leadership changes: new CFO, Deputy CEO's role change, and the pending universal bank licence approval.
Non-MFI and southern geography delinquency trends, which management did not quantify.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, liabilities and tech investments, but cautious on forward margins and credit cost. Management repeatedly said Q4 is seasonally strong and should not be annualised, and it gave no numeric guidance on the ECL impact or margins.
key_quotes: I wouldn't advise anybody that you should build our this quarter's credit cost as an overall cost for next year.
I don't think that 1.8 % this quarter ROA should be seen as our the permanent ROA because there are external challenges which we all know about.
So I think that's the two levers to watch out for next year and we'll see how we perform against these two.
The first benchmark should be that can I do around 3.5? And that too in three to four, three to five years, right?

adds.what: 80 to 100 new branches per year (2,790 touchpoints cited on call)
Retail secured distribution to about 900 to 1,000 branches per retail secured business (nearly doubled in two years)

growth.why: Management targets growth of 2 to 2.5x nominal GDP and guides FY27 credit cost around 90 bps and cost to assets below 4%, backed by 80 to 100 new branches a year and a secured-book shift; no revenue growth figure was guided and margin pressure is flagged for the next one to two quarters.
